rubrics.justification: Describes a good-quality expanded blastocyst with compact ICM, cohesive TE, and thinning zona consistent with the provided 3AA lab grade; notes the possible 3 vs 4 expansion nuance appropriately. Slight limitation because some image-specific details may be inferred from the reported grade.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, male factor context, prior live births/miscarriage, endometrial thickness, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: strong morphology and young age improve prognosis, while smoking, untested status, and prior miscarriage temper expectations. Probability range is well supported.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and aligned with IVF practice, including single embryo transfer, caution about morphology not equaling ploidy, and avoiding unproven add-ons. Minor soft spots include somewhat broad comments on stress and fresh-vs-frozen receptivity without case-specific hormone data.

Provides clear, practical next steps for the current transfer and future planning, including SET, smoking/alcohol cessation, luteal support adherence, review of embryology/transfer conditions, and when to consider further testing or PGT-A.
